newsitem.title: USA: Showers linger in eastern U.S. corn belt, west dry.
newsitem.headline: Showers linger in eastern U.S. corn belt, west dry.

text.p: Light, spotty showers were expected to linger in the eastern corn belt on Wednesday but cool, dry weather should prevail across the U.S. Midwest Thursday and Friday, meteorologists said.

"Tomorrow we should see some drier weather coming in," said Mike Palmerino, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "Along with that drier weather is going to come another round of cooler temperatures."
Freezing temperatures were reported in Springfield and Champaign, Ill., Wednesday morning. Other eastern Corn Belt areas recorded lows in the mid-30s to 40s Farenheit, he said.
Temperatures were expected to warm on Saturday with highs mostly in the 60s F, Palmerino said. A cold front was forecast to move in Saturday evening, bringing another round of light showers.

"Some light spotty showers will develop along this front as it moves across the region," said Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis. "Rainfall amounts will be .25 to .75 inch with 35 to 40 percent coverage of the belt.
"There is absolutely no indication of any kind of an extended period of wet weather developing across the Midwest during the next few weeks," Davis added.
The front could bring freezing temperatures to the central U.S. Midwest early next week, Palmerino said.

"That particular system is going to usher in potentially the coldest weather of the season so far," Palmerino said. "It has the potential to produce freezing temperatures through Iowa, central Illinois, Indiana and Ohio."
Long-range forecasts indicated a possible warm-up later next week but with the warmer temperatures came the chance of more showers, Palmerino said.
